name: General Dynamics
description: General Dynamics builds Gulfstream business jets, nuclear submarines and surface warships for the US Navy, combat vehicles and munitions, and defense IT and electronics. It is the only large defense prime in this group with a big commercial product: Gulfstream aircraft manufacturing is 18 percent of revenue, sold to companies, individuals and governments with deposits on order and the balance on delivery. The rest is mostly long-term US government contracts (68 percent of 2025 revenue), led by the Navy submarine programs (Virginia and Columbia class). Backlog was $118 billion at year-end 2025, up 30 percent in a year on $20.1 billion of submarine awards and $9.2 billion of international vehicle awards.

gics.note: Conventional label per Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-10-01), which gives only the sector and the sub-industry; GICS industry group and industry are not shown there so are left null. Mowgli classification is not set here.

employees.note: Approximately 117,000 employees; about 84% in the US. FY2025 10-K

businessLines.name: Marine Systems
businessLines.how: The US Navy pays under long-term cost-plus and fixed-price shipbuilding contracts, recognised as work is performed; revenue follows hours and material on multi-year hulls, and margin is thin (about 7 percent) and depends on contract performance.
businessLines.description: Nuclear submarines (Electric Boat: Virginia-class, Columbia-class), Arleigh Burke destroyers (Bath Iron Works), auxiliary and commercial ships, ship repair.

revenue.note: FY2024 $14,343M (+16.6%) on Virginia-class and Columbia-class submarine volume

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $14,343M (+16.6%) on Virginia-class and Columbia-class submarine volume

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $935M; 2026 outlook revenue $17.3-17.7B at about 7.3% margin

businessLines.name: Technologies
businessLines.how: Government agencies pay for IT services on cost-plus, time-and-materials and fixed-price contracts and for delivered electronics systems; mostly recurring multi-year work with revenue tied to staffed hours and program volume.
businessLines.description: GDIT (IT services, cyber and modernisation for defense, intelligence and civilian agencies) and Mission Systems (C5ISR electronics, encryption, undersea and space-ground systems).

revenue.note: FY2024 $13,127M (+2.6%); the increase was IT services +$296M and C5ISR +$48M

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $13,127M (+2.6%); the increase was IT services +$296M and C5ISR +$48M

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $1,260M; margin 9.5%; 2026 outlook revenue about $13.8B at about 9.2%

businessLines.name: Aerospace (Gulfstream)
businessLines.how: Customers (companies, individuals, governments) pay for each new jet, with deposits against orders and the balance on delivery; services add recurring maintenance and parts revenue on the installed fleet. Margin depends on ultra-large-cabin mix.
businessLines.description: Gulfstream business jets (G700, G800 and others) plus aircraft services: maintenance, repair, parts, pre-owned aircraft and fleet support.

revenue.note: Aircraft manufacturing $9,413M (FY2024 $7,811M), aircraft services $3,697M (FY2024 $3,438M); 158 Gulfstream deliveries vs 136 in 2024; FY2024 segment revenue $11,249M

businessLines.revenueNote: Aircraft manufacturing $9,413M (FY2024 $7,811M), aircraft services $3,697M (FY2024 $3,438M); 158 Gulfstream deliveries vs 136 in 2024; FY2024 segment revenue $11,249M

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $1,464M; margin 13.3% vs 13.0%; 2026 outlook revenue about $13.6B at about 14%

businessLines.name: Combat Systems
businessLines.how: The US Army and allied governments pay per vehicle and per round delivered under multi-year production and sustainment contracts; international vehicle orders ($9.2B awarded in 2025) and munitions demand drive volume.
businessLines.description: Abrams tanks, Stryker and wheeled armoured vehicles (incl. international customers), artillery, munitions and ordnance, weapon systems.
